channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Carney, Lula Forge Closer Ties With Forests Funding, Visits
item.description: Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney and Brazil’s President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva signaled closer ties on Sunday with funding to protect the world’s tropical forests and visits to each others’ countries.
item.dc:creator: Philip J. Heijmans

item.title: India Stock Market Rebounds as AI Trade Unwinds, Foreign Funds Return
item.description: Indian stocks suffered bruising losses in the first nine months of the year as the artificial intelligence trade hoovered up global investor capital. The unwinding of that strategy has turned the Asian nation’s equities into world beaters.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Vishnoi and Faseeh Mangi

item.title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
item.description: Jensen Huang’s leather jacket, traders busting out fax machines during the Outlook outage, mega paydays for AI talent, and first-class Frontier tickets for $129: Join Lisa Mateo, David Gura and Christina Ruffini for a roundup of headlines you may have missed, but gotta see. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Tools Huang Championed Now Star in Memes of His Downfall
item.description: Once artificial intelligence’s leading hype-man, Jensen Huang is now the face of an AI-driven meme craze.
item.dc:creator: Elena Eisenstadt

item.title: Anthropic IPO Tests Investor Appetite for AI
item.description: Bloomberg Technology co-host Ed Ludlow tells Bloomberg This Weekend why Anthropic’s upcoming IPO could be a major test of investor appetite for AI, with the offering heavily oversubscribed and poised to follow SpaceX’s blockbuster debut. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Ludlow also explains how Nvidia and Jensen Huang’s departure loom over the offering, given Nvidia’s planned investment in Anthropic and Huang’s central role connecting the companies powering the AI boom. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Italy Fines Meta €805 Million Over Access to Users’ Photos
item.description: The Italian Data Protection Authority fined Meta Platforms Inc. €805 million ($887 million) for accessing photos and videos of Android users’ galleries without their explicit consent.
item.dc:creator: Tiago Ramos Alfaro and Daniele Lepido

item.title: Nvidia Looks for a New Era After Huang
item.description: Bloomberg’s Emily Chang tells Bloomberg This Weekend what her recent interview with Jensen Huang reveals about Nvidia’s succession challenge after the longtime CEO’s abrupt departure. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Chang examines who could succeed Huang, the questions surrounding Nvidia’s China strategy and whether the AI giant can preserve the influence and relationships Huang built over more than three decades. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Couples Are Bringing AI Into Their Arguments
item.description: Bloomberg Weekend senior writer Morgan Meaker tells Bloomberg This Weekend how people are increasingly turning to AI chatbots for advice, validation and even mediation during arguments with their partners. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Meaker explores when AI can improve communication and when introducing a digital “third entity” risks creating distance between couples. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: “Bigger Than a Business Story”: Nvidia Shakeup
item.description: At the end of a week that saw revelations of ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s alleged affairs with employees and a suspected Chinese spy, Centerview Partners Senior Counselor Richard Haass says the national security implications go beyond the consequences for the company itself. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tech Giants Face More Grid Cost Pressure on Democratic Sweep
item.description: Tech giants chasing the infinite promise of AI are finding themselves increasingly on the hook for something far earthier — the electrical grid. A Democratic sweep will only intensify that.
item.dc:creator: Michelle Cheng and Dawn Lim

item.title: Nvidia’s Leadership Shakeup Tests AI Chip Giant
item.description: Bloomberg senior technology and strategic industries editor Mike Shepard tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Nvidia’s appointment of longtime CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO may offer investors some stability after Jensen Huang’s abrupt departure. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Shepard examines how Nvidia moves beyond a leader who defined the company for more than three decades and whether the upheaval creates an opening for AI chip rivals. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: My Husband and His Chatbot
item.description:
What happens when an AI chatbot becomes the third person in a marriage?
Morgan Meaker looks at whether algorithms are replacing the human friction real intimacy needs to survive. (Source: Bloomberg)
